clue.text: Game played from scratch

definitions.meaning: a board game where players build words from lettered tiles
to scratch or grope about with the hands and nails

explanation.surface: A game started from nothing, with no preparation at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played from' links the two senses; 'from scratch' reads as an idiom meaning from the beginning, hiding the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a famous tile-based word game and a verb for scrambling about with claws or fingers.

clue.text: Crumpled antique impounded by US agent

indicators.note: something impounded is shut inside, so the antique goes inside the agent

parts.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in American slang
antique means old

explanation.surface: A damaged antiquity has been seized by an American federal officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper that has been crumpled has been creased and bent over on itself.

clue.text: Small pub organised fine party

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters of fine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small pub has put on a good party.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinn Féin is an Irish republican political party; 'organised' turns FINE into FEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a political party active in Ireland and Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Find fault with small, not medium, snacks

parts.note: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: not says the medium letter is left out of the word for small

parts.note: mini means small
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A complaint about snacks being small rather than medium-sized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes M from MINI, leaving INI.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Italian toasted sandwiches, commonly eaten as light snacks.

clue.text: Part of store rebuilt outside centre of Lincoln

indicators.note: outside says the rebuilt letters go round the central letter
rebuilt means put together anew, so the letters of store are rearranged
centre of picks the middle letter of Lincoln

explanation.surface: A section of a shop is being rebuilt beyond the middle of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' turns STORE into SETOR, and 'outside' puts it round C, the middle letter of Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a part or division of a whole, such as a segment of an economy.

clue.text: Roosters standing on large unoccupied farm building

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
standing means upright, so in this down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: bats roost, hanging upside down, so they are roosters

indicators.note: unoccupied means emptied, leaving only the outside letters of large

explanation.surface: Cockerels perched on top of a large, empty barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roosters' suggests cockerels, but bats roost too; 'standing' reverses BATS to STAB, and 'unoccupied' empties large to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where horses are kept is a standard farm structure.

clue.text: Coarse knitting stitch used by a beginner finally unravelled

parts.note: rib is a knitting stitch making raised ridges
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of unravelled

explanation.surface: A rough piece of knitting made by a novice has come undone at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link joining the pieces; L for learner comes from British learner-driver L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse humour is vulgar and earthy, which is just what ribald jokes are.

clue.text: Sketches of Dutch boats

parts.note: rafts are simple boats

explanation.surface: Drawings of boats from the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Preliminary drawings or rough versions of a plan are both sketches.

clue.text: Two reps had relaxed, following introduction to Scottish union official

indicators.note: following places the rearranged letters after the Scottish initial
the introduction to a word is its first letter
relaxed suggests loosened from their order, so the letters of two reps had are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two union representatives unwound after a Scottish opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed' turns TWO REPS HAD into HOPSTEWARD, which 'following' puts after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A workplace representative elected by fellow trade-union members holds this official post.

clue.text: Stripe essential to shade of garment

indicators.note: essential to means at the heart of, so the stripe goes inside the shade

parts.note: a shade is a tad, a small amount
a bar is a stripe or band

explanation.surface: A stripe is key to the colour of an item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' looks like colour but means a tiny amount, TAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, such as the coat worn by heralds.

clue.text: Lecter or one of his ilk exchanging drugs

indicators.note: two drugs are swapped: cocaine (C) gives way to heroin (H)

parts.note: Lecter eats people, so one like him is a man-eater

explanation.surface: A villain or someone like him swapping narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: C and H are slang abbreviations for cocaine and heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannibal is the first name of Lecter, the fictional psychiatrist and serial killer.

clue.text: Hair arrangement hiding large lump

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so large goes inside the hairstyle

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A hairstyle concealing a big bump.
explanation.definitionFit: A blob is a small rounded mass, much like a lump of something soft.

clue.text: Time to stockpile drug before trading price leads to fall in value

indicators.note: to stockpile is to store up inside, so the date holds the other pieces

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: before puts the drug ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: E is ecstasy

indicators.note: trading suggests exchanging places, so the letters of price are rearranged

explanation.surface: Financial jargon: hoarding goods before prices move causes a drop in worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trading' looks like commerce but rearranges price to PRECI; 'leads to' is a link, and 'Time' is a calendar date, not T.
explanation.definitionFit: To depreciate is to lose worth over time, as cars and equipment do.

clue.text: Good money for registered nurse?

parts.note: something registered is official and lawful
to tend or nurse someone makes you their tender

explanation.surface: Asks whether a qualified nurse earns decent pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'registered nurse' reads as one job title but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency that must be accepted in payment of a debt is valid, genuine money.

clue.text: Went for alternative date to bury change of direction

indicators.note: to bury is to put inside, so the change of direction goes into the reworked letters
an alternative form of date means its letters rearranged

parts.note: to tack is a sailing change of course

explanation.surface: Someone chose another date so they could hide a course change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' turns DATE into ATED, and TACK is buried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for someone is to assault them, a common idiom for an assault.

clue.text: Calm child going first for church service

parts.note: even means calm and steady
a son is a child

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of going

explanation.surface: A quiet child heads off first to a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Anglican evening prayer service, often sung.

clue.text: Steers clear of second drama queen turning up to accept Oscar

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so Oscar goes inside
turning up in a down clue means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a diva is a temperamental star
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone shuns a second diva arriving to collect an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses S DIVA to AVIDS; O goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer clear of something is to keep away from it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Natural ability shown by experimental entertainer

indicators.note: shown by says the letters are on display within the following words

explanation.surface: An avant-garde performer displaying innate gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude or gift for something is a talent.

clue.text: Woman hoarding gold wrote badly in place of academic

indicators.note: hoarding means storing up inside, so gold goes inside the woman

parts.note: Ivy is a woman's name
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of wrote are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman stockpiling gold produced poor writing in place of a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'badly' turns WROTE into TOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a sheltered intellectual world detached from practical life, where scholars are said to live.

clue.text: Jacket worn for smoking?

parts.note: seems to describe a smoking jacket, but the same word names a thick double-breasted jacket and a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: Asks about a jacket you put on to smoke in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sailor's heavy short coat and a joint of cannabis.

clue.text: Space to accommodate host in Notting Hill, say

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the host goes inside

parts.note: room is space
an MC, master of ceremonies, is a host

explanation.surface: Space to house a host in a fashionable London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notting Hill' looks like the London district but is the 1999 film starring Hugh Grant and Julia Roberts.
explanation.definitionFit: That film is a classic example of a romantic comedy.

clue.text: Style of space outside city

indicators.note: outside means the space goes round the city

parts.note: an en is a printer's space
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Fashion from somewhere on the edge of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair or dash in manner is a kind of style.

clue.text: License crazy Republican to manufacture device for a gun

indicators.note: crazy means mad, so the letters of license are scrambled

explanation.surface: Allow an unhinged Republican to make gun attachments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to manufacture' is a link. 'crazy' turns LICENSE into SILENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A silencer is a muffling attachment fitted to a gun barrel.

clue.text: Lots of money given to fools

parts.note: asses are fools

explanation.surface: Loads of cash handed out to idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Large quantities or great numbers are referred to informally as lots.

clue.text: Asymmetrical sides of eager cook's equipment

parts.note: skew means slanted or lopsided

indicators.note: sides of takes the outer letters of eager

explanation.surface: Uneven parts of a keen chef's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pin used to hold kebabs or meat while cooking is a kitchen tool.

clue.text: Insect moving north-east

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word north plus E for east

explanation.surface: A bug heading off towards the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses NORTH spelled out plus E as the usual abbreviation of east.
explanation.definitionFit: A large stinging wasp is the insect in question.
